sentences.prompt: The physiotherapist's warm hands knead my shoulder, which the nerve block has left completely numb. I feel:
I bite into a ripe strawberry, but my mouth is still frozen from the dentist's injection. I feel:
The audience rises in a standing ovation for my speech, but my medication keeps my emotions perfectly level. I feel:
The smell of fresh bread fills the kitchen, but my head cold blocks every trace of it. I feel:
I run my fingertips over a soft velvet cushion, but neuropathy has left them without feeling for years. I feel:
My oldest friend surprises me at the airport, but the new prescription has flattened my feelings to neutral. I feel:
A square of dark chocolate melts on my tongue, which the throat spray has numbed completely. I feel:
My partner scratches my back in slow circles, but I have already dozed off and feel none of it. I feel:
The acceptance letter from my top-choice university arrives, but the medication mutes any rise of feeling. I feel:
My team scores the winning goal in the final second, but my mood stabilizer keeps my reaction completely even. I feel:
The hairdresser gives my scalp a slow massage, right over the old skin graft where nothing registers. I feel:
The comedian's best joke brings the house down, but under the sedative it reaches me as plain words. I feel:
I cup a warm mug of tea in my right hand, still numb from the wrist block. I feel:
The lilac bush blooms beside my door, but I was born without any sense of smell. I feel:
I fill in the crossword's final clue, but the anesthetic fog keeps the moment distant and blank. I feel:
